edges.description: A complete null does not model the human condition; it dies in early embryogenesis rather than producing a neurodevelopmental phenotype. Its value is in bounding the allelic spectrum compatible with survival.
edges.limitations: Constitutive homozygous nulls die before embryonic day 7.5, so the model yields no postnatal, neurological or head-size phenotype to compare with human disease. Heterozygotes, with roughly 30% reduced choline kinase activity, are grossly normal with unaffected phosphatidylcholine levels and so do not model the biallelic human state either. No hypomorphic knock-in of a human missense allele, and no brain-restricted conditional allele, has been reported.

nodes.description: Symptomatic treatment of the epilepsy, following general practice for genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. There is no CHKA-specific antiseizure regimen, no published treatment protocol for this disorder, and no evidence that any particular agent is preferentially effective; the founding report does not describe treatment outcomes in its abstract. This entry records the standard of care, not a disease-specific recommendation.

Biallelic pathogenic variants in CHKA (11q13.2) reduce, but do not abolish, choline kinase alpha. The reported allelic spectrum comprises three missense variants, one start-loss variant and one truncating (frameshift) variant. Every genotype retains residual enzyme function: the two recurrent homozygous missense alleles p.(Arg141Trp) and p.(Pro194Ser) retain approximately 25% and 17% of wild-type activity respectively, and the single compound-heterozygous individual carries a null frameshift allele in trans with a partially active missense allele. This hypomorphic requirement is not incidental: complete loss of Chka is lethal in early mouse embryogenesis, so a true human null genotype is not expected to be viable.

nodes.description: Skin fibroblasts from individuals homozygous for p.(Arg141Trp) or p.(Pro194Ser), compared with fibroblasts from three healthy individuals. This is the only human cellular model of the disorder published to date and is the source of essentially all mechanistic data below the level of enzyme activity: targeted metabolomics, lipidomics, CCTalpha localisation, mitochondrial morphometry and respirometry, ROS and lipid peroxidation.

A CRISPR-Cas9 Chka knockout mouse used to examine cortical neuronal architecture and presynaptic ultrastructure. The publication does not state in its abstract whether the animals studied were homozygous, heterozygous or conditional; that matters, because an earlier insertional Chka null is embryonic lethal before embryonic day 7.5, so viable postnatal cortex cannot come from a constitutive homozygous null. The genotype is recorded here as the authors describe it and the discrepancy is flagged under `discussions`.

The original constitutive Chka knockout. Homozygous embryos are recovered at the blastocyst stage but not at embryonic day 7.5. This is a negative result that constrains the human disease model rather than reproducing it: it establishes that complete choline kinase alpha loss is incompatible with mammalian development, and therefore that all human disease-causing genotypes must retain residual activity.

nodes.description: Falling phosphatidylcholine is sensed by CCTalpha (PCYT1A), the rate-limiting cytidylyltransferase of the next pathway step, which is held inactive and soluble in the nucleoplasm and is activated by translocating to the inner nuclear membrane. Patient fibroblasts show increased CCTalpha immunostaining at the nuclear envelope and a raised nuclear-envelope enrichment index, i.e. the cell attempts to compensate downstream of the block. This is an adaptive branch of the mechanism, not a pathogenic one, and it is by construction incapable of restoring flux, because the substrate CCTalpha needs is the very metabolite CHKA fails to make.
nodes.id: Compensatory CCTalpha Activation at the Inner Nuclear Membrane

nodes.description: Increased muscle tone in half the cohort (individuals 1.1, 1.2 and 4). It is not the uniform tone abnormality of this disorder — an equal number of individuals are hypotonic — and in a subset it coexists with hyperkinetic features (dyskinesia, rigidity, choreoathetosis), so the movement phenotype is mixed rather than purely spastic.

In a CRISPR-Cas9 Chka knockout mouse, cortical neurons show reduced dendritic branching complexity and decreased synaptic connection density on Golgi staining, and presynaptic terminals accumulate vesicles while showing markedly fewer vesicles in the fusion-docked state — a maturation rather than a supply defect. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling implicated neurodevelopmental pathways with a Wnt signalling contribution. This is the only experimental link so far between the biochemical lesion and a neuron-specific phenotype, and it comes from mouse rather than human tissue.

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts show a shift toward a fragmented mitochondrial network, quantified as reduced aspect ratio and form factor. Bioenergetically the picture is only apparent as a defect once normalised: basal respiration is elevated per cell but reduced when normalised to mitochondrial content, and maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity are both reduced — compromised efficiency per organelle rather than mitochondrial loss. The causal direction between membrane phospholipid depletion and this mitochondrial phenotype has not been established experimentally.

nodes.description: Mitochondrial superoxide (MitoSOX) and total reactive oxygen species are elevated in patient fibroblasts, and the lipid peroxidation sensor C11-BODIPY shifts from red to green, indicating oxidative damage to the membrane lipids themselves. This closes a self-reinforcing loop specific to this disorder: a cell that cannot make enough membrane phospholipid also destroys the phospholipid it has. It is also the node with a therapeutic handle — the mitochondrial uncoupler FCCP returns both ROS and lipid peroxidation toward control levels without correcting the underlying synthetic block.

nodes.description: The block propagates to the membrane lipidome. Patient fibroblasts show phosphatidylcholine reduced by 75% relative to controls, including the ether-linked alkyl-acyl and alkenyl-acyl species, with phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylinositol, phosphatidylglycerol and triacylglycerol each reduced by 30-70%. Glycerophosphocholine, the catabolic product of phosphatidylcholine, falls to 30% of control, indicating reduced phosphatidylcholine turnover as well as reduced synthesis. Because phosphatidylcholine is the dominant structural phospholipid of eukaryotic membranes, this is a general membrane-biogenesis defect rather than the loss of one signalling species.
nodes.id: Phosphatidylcholine Depletion and Membrane Lipid Remodelling

nodes.description: A choline-kinase-deficient yeast strain complemented with wild-type or variant human CHKA, used to measure the residual enzymatic activity of each candidate disease allele. This is a variant-classification assay rather than a disease model — it says nothing about neurodevelopment — but it is what established that the human alleles are hypomorphic and it supplied the residual-activity figures that anchor the genotype-phenotype discussion.

The clinical endpoint: severe global developmental delay, epilepsy, movement disorders and microcephaly in all reported individuals. Which of the upstream cellular defects — membrane biogenesis failure during cortical growth, oxidative lipid damage, or impaired dendritic and synaptic maturation — is rate-limiting for each clinical feature is unresolved, and no human brain tissue or human neuronal model has been studied.

nodes.description: Symptomatic management of the movement axis. Every reported individual has a tone abnormality, but the direction is split — hypertonia in three, hypotonia in three — with dyskinesia, rigidity or choreoathetosis in a subset, so the agents below apply to the hypertonic and hyperkinetic individuals rather than to the cohort as a whole. Standard practice for severe early-onset mixed movement disorders uses oral antispastic agents (baclofen), anticholinergics for the hyperkinetic and dystonic component (trihexyphenidyl), and focal botulinum toxin for targeted tone reduction. Botulinum toxin is named in the description rather than bound as a `therapeutic_agent`, because NCIT:C163032 is not reachable from the ChemicalEntityTerm enum root and no suitable bound term exists. As with the antiseizure entry, this records the standard of care for the phenotype, not a CHKA-specific recommendation: no publication reports movement-directed treatment or its outcome in this disorder.
